key_insight: PEA spacers improve crystal morphology and reduce lattice defects in two-dimensional lead iodide perovskites, slowing degradation under ambient light and thermal stress compared with BA spacers.
engineering_relevance: Spacer selection can improve perovskite durability, but long-term device stability also requires structural and chemical engineering, surface passivation, and encapsulation.
method: Compared BA₂PbI₄ and PEA₂PbI₄ exfoliated nanoflakes.
Assessed ambient photo- and thermal stability using confocal micro-Raman spectroscopy.
Probed chemical degradation using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy.
evidence_signal: Fresh nanoflakes showed comparable room-temperature luminescence, while PEA-based crystals degraded more slowly; both materials lost organic components and decomposed into PbI₂ and metallic Pb.
watch_item: The abstract reports material-level stability rather than solar-cell efficiency or operational lifetime, and describes no AI method.
paper_title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites
